knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A small disagreement is easier to resolve before it grows. Naming it early is the leader's job.
A mediator hears both sides, restates the facts neutrally and keeps their own view out of it.
Pricing changes are outside the lead's authority in this lesson, so the lead refers them to the supervisor.
The choosing battles section says not every disagreement is worth a formal process.

practicalCriteria: The learner runs a role-play mediation in which each side is heard separately before the joint discussion and the facts are restated neutrally.
The learner writes one agreed step with an owner and a check date, and identifies at least one matter to refer to the supervisor.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Dispute record with agreed step and check date
stopWorkCriteria: Stop the work and refer to the supervisor where a dispute creates an immediate safety risk.
Stop and refer any dispute involving harassment or discrimination to the business's procedure.
